projects.name: ff-jarvis
projects.hook: A fantasy football model that tests popular draft narratives against 15 seasons of data and keeps only the ones that win. Powers the Draft War Room and Team Watch.

headline.label: points a season over drafting by ADP, in simulated drafts 2011 to 2025; ahead in 12 of 15 seasons

clips.alt: The draft board on a phone: a pick lands and the board re-ranks.

points: Data from ESPN, Yahoo, Sleeper, nflverse, betting props and weather, pulled nightly.
Backtested in simulated 12-team drafts on the 2011 to 2025 seasons.
A Python pipeline turns 15 seasons of draft and stat data into one JSON file the React board loads.
The pick engine is pure JavaScript, so the board re-ranks in the browser after every pick, no server.
The same engine can draft for you, running 30 full drafts from your seat in a few seconds, every strategy on the same random draws.

projects.name: Team Watch
projects.hook: Your fantasy stats, start/sit calls and player breakdowns in one place, powered by ff-jarvis.

clips.alt: Team Watch on a phone: Jahmyr Gibbs's profile, where tapping his stat sphere opens it into a radar of his RB ranks.
Team Watch on a phone: the week's roster pack tears open and the cards come out, worst first, best last.

points: Claude writes the words and Python checks them. A number that isn't in the data sends the reply back once, then it's replaced with plain facts.
For game previews, Claude predicts each game before it sees the betting line, and every pick is graded against the final score.
For highlights, Claude picks from a shortlist Python builds, and each line is checked against that player's numbers.
For the league roast, one Claude pass drafts and a second ranks, and the best draft that passes the checks ships.
The pack tear follows your finger, with drag progress driving the CSS variables that peel the foil.
The stat crystal is hand-rolled 3D on a 2D canvas, and a tap tilts it flat into a radar chart.

projects.name: Restock Watch
projects.hook: Pings Discord when sealed Pokémon, One Piece or Riftbound product restocks at 7 big retailers, and flags whether the price is fair or a scalper's markup.

clips.alt: Restock Watch on a phone: the status page and its price tiles.

points: Each retailer gets its own method, from Best Buy's official API to Walmart's embedded page data to Target read inside a real Chrome.
Prices each restock against retail, with TCGplayer for market value.
Within 10% of retail is an urgent Discord ping; above that, a quiet one.
A hot score ranks products by market premium, product type, Reddit buzz and stock state.

projects.name: Seat Scout
projects.hook: Finds the best seats still open for selected showings in California.

clips.alt: Seat Scout on a phone during its September 2026 run: open-seat counts per theater, then a theater's best bets as Admit One ticket stubs.

points: Reads seat maps from inside a real Chrome session over the DevTools protocol.
Seats are tiered Center, Mid-back or Edge by depth and side; the front 30% of rows never count.
A run of n open seats together yields floor(n/2) pairs, each rated by its worse seat.
The public page shows counts only, sorted by distance from you. A Discord bot scans when @mentioned.

projects.name: Team Lock
projects.hook: A fantasy football auto-battler. Build a roster, call plays, and lead your team to the championship.

clips.alt: Team Lock: the wide receiver, falling right, reaches one-handed for the ball.
Team Lock storyboard: the whole lineup lights up and links, then LOCKED IN over the roll call.

points: A Python simulator plays out each down from seeded rules that switch on and off.
The animation runs on a Spine-style 2D rigging engine built from scratch, where each drawing is cut into parts and each part is a PixiJS mesh bent every frame.
Springs give soft parts follow-through, and two-bone IK keeps planted feet on the ground.
Motion is layered pulses with smoothstep easing, not keyframes.
Character art comes from a ComfyUI pipeline.
